title.en: Dynasty Challenge: 4,000 Years on One Map
title.zh: 朝代大挑战：一张地图看四千年

clips.send: Republic of China (1912–1949). 1912–1949. 1912: no more emperors. On 1 January 1912 the Republic of China was founded in Nanjing, with Sun Yat-sen as provisional president. The 1911 Revolution (辛亥革命) overthrew Qing and ended over 2,000 years of rule by emperors. The period was full of struggle: warlords, the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression (1931–1945) and civil war.

clips.send: Xia. c. 2070–1600 BCE. Father to son: the first hereditary throne. When Yu’s son Qi inherited the throne, “all under heaven” became one family’s business. That rule — the throne stays in the family — lasted 4,000 years. Around 2070 BCE Yu founded Xia — the textbook’s first dynasty. Before Xia, leaders were chosen by merit (“abdication”, 禅让 shànràng). After Yu, his son Qi took the throne, and power stayed in the family.

clips.send: Northern Song, Liao, Western Xia. Northern Song 960–1127. The Chanyuan Treaty (1005). After a war, Song and Liao made peace: Song paid silver and silk each year, and the two sides traded peacefully for over 100 years. Bi Sheng (毕昇) invented movable-type printing. In Sichuan, merchants began using jiaozi (交子), the world’s earliest paper money.

clips.send: Yuan. 1271–1368. The province system (行省制度). Yuan divided its huge empire into provinces (行省 xíngshěng). It was the start of China’s province system — the “provinces” on today’s map come from it. Kublai Khan named his dynasty Yuan in 1271. Yuan took Lin’an in 1276 and finished off the last Song resistance in 1279. The Xuanzheng Yuan (宣政院) governed Tibet; a Penghu inspectorate (澎湖巡检司) managed Penghu and Liuqiu (today’s Taiwan).

clips.send: Eastern Jin and Sixteen Kingdoms. Eastern Jin 317–420. Battle of the Fei River (383). Former Qin (前秦), which had united the north, attacked with a huge army. The smaller Eastern Jin army won — and gave Chinese the idiom “every tree and blade of grass looks like a soldier” (草木皆兵). In the north many regimes rose and fell — the “Sixteen Kingdoms” (十六国). Huge numbers of northerners moved south, bringing farming skills; the Jiangnan region (south of the Yangtze) began to boom.

clips.send: Three Kingdoms. 220–280. After Red Cliffs: a three-way split. In 208 Sun Quan and Liu Bei together beat Cao Cao’s bigger army at Red Cliffs (赤壁) — with fire ships and smart use of wind and river. It set up the three-way split. Wei was founded in 220, Shu in 221, Wu in 222 — “three legs of a cauldron” (三国鼎立). Zhuge Liang (诸葛亮) ran Shu. In 230 Wu’s ruler Sun Quan sent a fleet to Yizhou (today’s Taiwan; 夷洲).

clips.send: Western Zhou. 1046–771 BCE. The enfeoffment system (分封制). The Zhou king gave land and people to relatives and heroes, making them lords (诸侯 zhūhóu) who guarded the realm and sent tribute — a bit like medieval Europe’s lords and vassals. In 1046 BCE King Wu beat the Shang army at the Battle of Muye (牧野之战). In 771 BCE the Quanrong (犬戎) captured Haojing and Western Zhou ended.

clips.send: Western Han. 202 BCE – 8 CE. Zhang Qian opens the Silk Road. In 138 BCE Zhang Qian (张骞) set off west — and was captured for over ten years before getting home. His trips opened the Silk Road, linking Chang’an to Central Asia and on towards Rome. Emperor Wu (汉武帝) made Han strongest and made Confucianism the official teaching (罢黜百家, 尊崇儒术). In 60 BCE Han set up the Protector-General of the Western Regions (西域都护) — today’s Xinjiang came under the central government from then on.

clips.send: Tang. 618–907. A golden age: Chang’an, world city. Under Emperor Taizong (the “Zhenguan reign”) and Emperor Xuanzong (the “Kaiyuan golden age”), Chang’an held about a million people — merchants, monks and students from across Asia. 641: Princess Wencheng (文成公主) travelled to Tibet to marry the Tubo king Songtsen Gampo (松赞干布). 755: the An–Shi Rebellion (安史之乱) began — the turning point from glory to decline.

clips.send: People’s Republic of China (1949–). 1949 – today. 1949: New China. The founding of the PRC opened a new era in Chinese history. On 1 October 1949 Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People’s Republic of China in Tiananmen Square. At 77 years old, the PRC is younger than the USA (250).

clips.send: Ming. 1368–1644. Zheng He sails seven times (1405–1433). Admiral Zheng He (郑和) led fleets of up to 200+ ships as far as East Africa — decades before Columbus. Emperor Yongle moved the capital to Beijing in 1421 and built the Forbidden City. Ming rebuilt the Great Wall in brick and stone, from the Yalu River to Jiayu Pass.

clips.send: Eastern Zhou. 770–256 BCE (Spring and Autumn 770–476, Warring States 475–221). Seven states, a hundred schools of thought. War pushed change: iron tools, new laws, and thinkers like Confucius, Mozi, Laozi and Han Fei arguing about how to run a country — the “Hundred Schools of Thought”. Spring and Autumn (770–476 BCE): strong lords competed to be “hegemon”. Confucius (孔子) taught. Warring States (475–221 BCE): seven big states. Shang Yang’s reforms (商鞅变法) made Qin the strongest; Li Bing (李冰) built the Dujiangyan irrigation system.

clips.send: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms. 907–960 (Five Dynasties). Five dynasties in 53 years. The north changed hands five times while about ten smaller kingdoms ruled the south. The south saw less war, so its farms and towns kept growing. In the north, Later Liang, Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han and Later Zhou followed one another in just 53 years. 916: the Khitan (契丹 Qìdān) leader Abaoji founded the state later called Liao; in 938 it gained the Sixteen Prefectures of Yan–Yun, including today’s Beijing.

clips.send: Western Jin. 266–316. 280: China reunited — for a while. Jin conquered Wu in 280 and ended 60 years of division. It lasted about 35 years before the north broke apart again. In 266 Sima Yan took the throne from Wei and founded Jin. The unity was short: princes fought each other, rebellions broke out, and Western Jin fell in 316.

clips.send: Southern Song, Jin. Southern Song 1127–1279. Yue Fei fights Jin; the economy moves south. General Yue Fei (岳飞) won big victories against Jin. Meanwhile the south grew richer than the north — by Southern Song, China’s economic centre had moved south for good. 1142: Song and Jin made peace, with a border along the Huai River and Dasan Pass (大散关). “When Suzhou and Huzhou have a good harvest, the whole country has enough” (苏湖熟, 天下足).

clips.send: Sui. 581–618. The Grand Canal and the imperial exams. Sui dug the Grand Canal to move grain from the rich south to the north, and began choosing officials by exam instead of by family — the imperial examinations (科举 kējǔ). 589: Sui conquered Chen and reunited China after almost 300 years of division. The Grand Canal ran 2,000+ km (1,240+ mi) from Zhuojun (today’s Beijing) to Yuhang (today’s Hangzhou), centred on Luoyang — about New York to Miami.

clips.send: Northern and Southern Dynasties. 420–589. Emperor Xiaowen’s reforms. In 494 Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei (a Xianbei 鲜卑 ruler) moved his capital to Luoyang and had his court adopt Han clothes, language and surnames — a big step in the blending of peoples. The south had four dynasties in a row — Song, Qi, Liang, Chen — all ruling from Jiankang. Zu Chongzhi (祖冲之) calculated pi to between 3.1415926 and 3.1415927 — the world’s best for about 1,000 years.

clips.send: Eastern Han. 25–220. Cai Lun improves paper (105 CE). Cai Lun (蔡伦) made paper from bark, hemp, rags and old fishing nets — cheap and light. Paper became one of China’s Four Great Inventions. Zhang Heng (张衡) built a seismoscope (地动仪) that showed the direction of distant earthquakes. Ban Chao (班超) restored Han control in the Western Regions; Buddhism arrived from India.

clips.send: Qin. 221–207 BCE. 221 BCE: China is unified. Qin conquered the other six states in ten years and created China’s first unified, centralised state ruled by an emperor. Qin itself lasted only 15 years — but its systems lasted 2,000. He called himself the “First Emperor” (始皇帝) and ran the country through commanderies and counties (郡县制 jùnxiànzhì) led by officials he appointed. One script (small seal 小篆), one round coin with a square hole, one set of weights and measures — and the Great Wall joined up.

clips.send: Shang. c. 1600–1046 BCE. Pan Geng moves the capital to Yin. Around 1300 BCE King Pan Geng moved the capital to Yin. Shang settled down there for the rest of the dynasty — and Yin’s ruins (殷墟) later gave up thousands of oracle bones. Shang kings asked their ancestors questions by cracking turtle shells and ox bones. The answers were carved on them: oracle-bone script (甲骨文), the oldest mature Chinese writing. The Houmuwu ding (后母戊鼎) weighs 832.84 kg (1,836 lb) — more than a grand piano. It is the heaviest ancient bronze vessel found in China.

clips.send: Qing. 1644–1912 (name Qing from 1636). Kangxi: Taiwan and the Russian border. In 1683 Qing brought Taiwan under its rule and in 1684 set up Taiwan Prefecture. In 1689 the Treaty of Nerchinsk (尼布楚条约) with Russia set the northeast border. Emperor Qianlong put down revolts in Xinjiang in the 1750s and secured Qing rule there. 1840: the Opium War — the start of modern Chinese history. 1912: the last emperor abdicated.

clips.send: 西汉。公元前202—公元8年。张骞通西域，开辟丝绸之路。前138年，张骞出使西域，途中被匈奴扣留十多年。他两次出使，打通了从长安经河西走廊、西域通往西亚、欧洲的丝绸之路。汉武帝时国力强盛，“罢黜百家，尊崇儒术”。公元前60年，西汉设立西域都护，标志着今新疆地区开始隶属于中央政权。

clips.send: 南北朝。公元420—589年。北魏孝文帝改革。494年，北魏孝文帝迁都洛阳，推行汉化改革：穿汉服、说汉语、改汉姓、与汉族通婚，促进了民族交融。南朝先后经历宋、齐、梁、陈四个朝代，都以建康为都城。祖冲之把圆周率精确到3.1415926和3.1415927之间，领先世界近千年。

clips.send: 中华民国（1912—1949年）。1912—1949年。1912年：中华民国成立。1912年1月1日，中华民国在南京成立，孙中山就任临时大总统。辛亥革命推翻了清王朝，结束了统治中国两千多年的君主专制制度。这一时期经历了军阀割据、抗日战争（1931—1945年）和解放战争。

clips.send: 东周。公元前770—前256年（春秋前770—前476年，战国前475—前221年）。战国七雄与百家争鸣。社会大变革推动了思想繁荣：儒家、道家、墨家、法家等学派相互争辩，形成“百家争鸣”的局面。春秋时期（前770—前476年）：诸侯争霸；孔子创立儒家学派。战国时期（前475—前221年）：齐、楚、燕、韩、赵、魏、秦并称“战国七雄”；商鞅变法使秦国逐渐强大；李冰主持修建都江堰。

clips.send: 五代十国。公元907—960年。“五代”与“十国”。北方政权更替频繁，南方等地先后出现十个割据政权。南方战乱较少，经济继续发展。北方先后出现后梁、后唐、后晋、后汉、后周五个政权，只有53年。916年，契丹首领阿保机建立契丹国（后改称辽）；938年，后晋把燕云十六州割给契丹。

clips.send: 夏。约公元前2070—前1600年。“家天下”：王位世袭制开始。启继承王位，“公天下”变成了“家天下”。王位世袭制此后沿用了几千年。约公元前2070年，禹建立夏朝，这是我国历史上第一个王朝。夏朝以前实行禅让制；禹死后，他的儿子启继承王位，王位世袭制代替了禅让制。

clips.send: 秦。公元前221—前207年。前221年：秦统一六国。秦用十年时间灭掉六国，建立起我国历史上第一个统一的多民族的中央集权国家。秦朝只存在了15年，但它的制度影响了两千多年。嬴政自称“始皇帝”，在地方推行郡县制，官员由皇帝任免。统一文字（小篆）、货币（圆形方孔钱）和度量衡；修筑长城，开凿灵渠。

clips.send: 清。公元1644—1912年（1636年改国号为清）。康熙帝统一台湾、抗击沙俄。1683年清军进入台湾，1684年设台湾府；1689年中俄签订《尼布楚条约》，从法律上确定了中俄东段边界。乾隆帝平定准噶尔和大小和卓叛乱，巩固了对新疆的管辖。1840年鸦片战争爆发，中国近代史开始；1912年清帝退位。

clips.send: 商。约公元前1600—前1046年。盘庚迁殷。约公元前1300年，商王盘庚迁都到殷，商朝从此稳定下来。殷墟出土了大量甲骨文和青铜器。商朝人用龟甲和兽骨占卜，并把卜辞刻在上面，这就是甲骨文——目前已知我国最早的成熟文字。后母戊鼎重832.84千克，是目前已知我国古代最重的青铜器。
